newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel does not know who behind bombings - official.
newsitem.headline: Israel does not know who behind bombings - official.

text.p: Israel has doubts a Hamas claim of responsibility for a double suicide bombing that killed 13 people is authentic and is not certain who carried out the attack, an official said on Thursday.

"We for the time being cannot say who was responsible for the attack," said the Israeli official briefing reporters about the investigation of Wednesday's twin blasts that ripped through an outdoor Jerusalem market injuring 170 peopele.
"There was a leaflet in Ramallah. Basically, it seems authentic but we are not sure," said the official, who refused to be named.
A leaflet in the name of the Islamic Hamas group on Wednesday claimed responsibility for the bombings and warned of more attacks unless Israel released jailed Islamic militants.

Israel has so far failed to identify the two bombers. The official said there was only a "remote possibility" their bodies were those of two Islamic militants from the Dahariyeh village in the West Bank who have been missing for 15 months.
Israeli forces detained members of their two families on Thursday.
"It's not difficult to assume that this is a radical Islamic organisation but there are many candidates for that," the official said.

Israeli security officials met late on Wednesday with Jibril Rajoub and Mohammad Dahlan -- Palestinian preventive security chiefs in the West Bank and Gaza -- in what the official described as a resumption of security contacts severed in March.
But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had done "damn all" to stop Palestinian militants.
Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement four months ago in East Jerusalem -- the heart of Arab-Israeli feuding -- deadlocked Israel-PLO peacemaking and touched off waves of violence.
Hamas and the smaller Islamic Jihad groups have spearheaded opposition to Israel-PLO peace deals, killing scores of Israelis in suicide bombings since 1994.
Israelis braced for more attacks on Thursday, recalling four bombings by Islamic militants in the span of nine days last year in which 57 people were killed in the Jewish state.
